title: Sagrada Familia
blurb: Antoni Gaudi’s unfinished basilica in Barcelona, in simplified schematic form: the Latin-cross plan, its forest of branching columns, and the planned 18 spires rising to 172.5 m, the tallest church tower in the world since February 2026.

Sagrada Familia official booklet 8: Glory Facade
Popular Science: Tower of Jesus completed February 2026

systems.name: Spires
systems.description: The planned 18 spires: twelve apostles at 100 m, four evangelists at 135 m, the Virgin Mary at 138 m and Jesus Christ at 172.5 m.

systems.name: Facades
systems.description: The three great facades: Nativity in the northeast facing the sunrise, Passion in the southwest facing the sunset, and Glory in the south as the main entrance.

systems.name: Nave and columns
systems.description: The forest of branching tree-like columns on a 7.5 m grid that carries the vaults without flying buttresses.

systems.name: Vaults
systems.description: Hyperboloid and barrel vaults from 30 m in the aisles to 75 m in the apse.

systems.name: Apse
systems.description: Seven chapels ringing the apse behind the ambulatory.

systems.name: Cloister and crypt
systems.description: The cloister surrounding the church and the crypt foundations below.

explanations.nativity apostle spires: Four of the twelve apostle spires, each rising to 100 m on the Nativity Facade in the northeast, facing the sunrise. Exact shaft profiles are schematic.
explanations.passion apostle spires: Four of the twelve apostle spires, each rising to 100 m on the Passion Facade in the southwest, facing the sunset. Exact shaft profiles are schematic.
explanations.glory apostle spires: Four of the twelve apostles spires on the Glory Facade; on the street side these rise from about 30 m up on the beatitude columns. The Glory spires are not yet built. Exact profiles are schematic.
explanations.matthew spire (angel): One of four evangelist spires at 135 m, crowned by the angel of Matthew. Exact sculpture is schematic.
explanations.mark spire (lion): One of four evangelist spires at 135 m, crowned by the lion of Mark. Exact sculpture is schematic.
explanations.luke spire (ox): One of four evangelist spires at 135 m, crowned by the ox of Luke. Exact sculpture is schematic.
explanations.john spire (eagle): One of four evangelist spires at 135 m, crowned by the eagle of John. Exact sculpture is schematic.
explanations.jesus christ spire: The Tower of Jesus Christ rises to 172.5 m, the tallest church tower in the world since its exterior was completed on 20 February 2026. It rests on four monumental porphyry columns at the crossing. Exact profile is schematic.
explanations.jesus spire cross: The four-armed cross crowning the basilica, 17 m tall and 13.5 m wide, built in Germany in 2025.
explanations.virgin mary spire: The Tower of the Virgin Mary rises to 138 m, inaugurated in December 2021, crowned by a twelve-pointed crown and the morning star. Exact profile is schematic.
explanations.nativity facade: The Nativity Facade wall on the northeast side, facing the sunrise, built under Gaudi direct supervision. Exact massing is schematic.
explanations.nativity portals: The three portals of the Nativity Facade, representing the theological virtues of Charity, Hope and Faith. Exact portal layout is schematic.
explanations.passion facade: The Passion Facade on the southwest side, facing the sunset, with six inward-slanting bone-like columns carrying an austere sculptural program of the final days of Christ. Exact angles are schematic.
explanations.passion portals: The three bronze portals of the Passion Facade. Exact panel divisions are schematic.
explanations.glory facade: The Glory Facade on the south side, the main entrance facing the sea, with its great narthex carried on columns for the eight beatitudes. Under construction and shown as designed.
explanations.glory doors: The seven bronze doors of the Glory Facade, representing the seven corporal works of mercy. Under construction and shown as designed.
explanations.west nave columns: Branching tree-like columns of the nave, part of the forest of columns that carries the vaults without flying buttresses. Columns stand on a 7.5 m grid. Exact branch geometry is schematic.
explanations.east nave columns: Branching tree-like columns of the nave, part of the forest of columns that carries the vaults without flying buttresses. Columns stand on a 7.5 m grid. Exact branch geometry is schematic.
explanations.crossing columns: Four monumental porphyry columns at the crossing, carrying the Tower of Jesus Christ. Exact positions are schematic.
explanations.west nave wall: The west outer wall of the nave above the side aisles. Exact wall articulation is schematic.
explanations.east nave wall: The east outer wall of the nave above the side aisles. Exact wall articulation is schematic.
explanations.central nave vault: The central nave vault, rising to 45 m over the five-aisled nave. Exact profile is schematic.
explanations.west aisle vault: The west side aisle vault at 30 m. Exact profile is schematic.
explanations.east aisle vault: The east side aisle vault at 30 m. Exact profile is schematic.
explanations.transept vault: The transept vault at 60 m over the crossing arms. Exact profile is schematic.
explanations.crossing hyperboloid: The great hyperboloid at the crossing, surrounded by two rings of twelve hyperboloids. Exact geometry is schematic.
explanations.apse wall: The apse outer wall. Exact massing is schematic.
explanations.apse chapels: The seven chapels of the apse, opening onto the ambulatory. Exact chapel widths are schematic.
explanations.apse ambulatory: The ambulatory ringing the apse behind the chapels. Exact layout is schematic.
explanations.apse vault: The apse hyperboloid vault rising to 75 m, the tallest interior vault of the church. Exact profile is schematic.
explanations.cloister: The cloister surrounding the church, a layout completely original in Christian architecture, isolating the church from the outside. Exact segment lengths are schematic.
explanations.chapel of the assumption: The Chapel of the Assumption in the apse section of the cloister. Exact placement is schematic.
explanations.crypt: The crypt and its foundations below the apse; gaps in the apse floor open down to it. Exact layout is schematic.
